questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

Although not all those who study

A-better thinkers and leaders

B-become philosophers, they become

C-logic or philosophy may
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'CBA'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the fixed sentence, the last word is 'study' hence, after we need to write an object that can be a noun/pronoun/gerund the noun is written only in the 'C' part i.e. 'logic' hence it will be the first part.
 
• 'may' is the last word of the first part hence after this we need a main verb which is written in part 'b' i.e. 'become'
 
• So according to the correct logic is- CBA
 
 
• *Although not all those who study logic or philosophy may become philosophers, they become better thinkers and leaders.*

questions.question:
**In the following question out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement in needed , select “no improvement”.**

If all of us (had been) philosophical thinkers, we would not have been deceived by scheming politicians all these years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'No improvement'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to grammar, the given sentence is a conditional sentence of the third type in which the structure is- If + had + V₃... Subject + would + have + V₃.
 
• Hence, according to this structure, the given sentence is correct.
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• If it had rained, you would have gotten wet.
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-** *If all of us **had been** philosophical thinkers, we would not have been deceived by scheming politicians all these years.*

options.text: The President shot by the assassin.

__
 
• In the given sentence, the subject is 'the assassin' and the object is 'the president'
 
• The verb of the sentence is 'shot' that is in the past tense. Hence, in the passive voice, the tense remains the same.
 
• So, in the passive voice, the object of the sentence becomes the subject and the subject becomes the object.

**So the correct passive is- ***The President was shot by the assassin.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Peer
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Inferior'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct answer for the word opposite in meaning to** "Peer"** is: **Inferior.**
 
• The word "**Peer**" refers to **someone who is equal in social status, age, or abilities.** It indicates a person who belongs to the same group or level as others, often implying a sense of similarity or equality.
 
 
• For example, if two individuals are of the same age and have similar qualifications, they can be considered peers.
 
 
 
• On the other hand, "**Inferior**" is the opposite of "**Peer**." It means **lower in rank, status, quality, or ability.** When someone is referred to as inferior, it suggests that they are of a lower position or level compared to others. For instance, if one person is highly skilled and accomplished while another is less experienced and less competent, the latter can be considered inferior to the former.
 
• Now, let's examine the other options:
 
• **Equal**: This option is not the opposite of "Peer" but rather a synonym. "Equal" refers to someone or something that is the same in quantity, degree, value, or status. It indicates a sense of similarity or equivalence.
 
• Look: This option does not represent the opposite meaning of "Peer." "Look" can refer to the act of visually perceiving something or the physical appearance of someone. It does not carry an opposite meaning in relation to "Peer."
 
• **Match**: This option does not convey the opposite meaning of "Peer" either. "Match" can refer to something that corresponds or goes well with another thing. It can also refer to a competition or contest between two individuals or teams.
 
• To summarize, the correct opposite for "**Peer**" is "**Inferior**," as it denotes a lower rank or position. The other options, "Equal," "Look," and "Match," do not represent the opposite meaning of "Peer" but rather carry different meanings.

• **In option 3, **'complete' is an adjective but we cannot use this because this makes the sentence contextually incorrect because we are talking about 'without education' hence, it doesn't make any sense that 'without education we are complete' so this option is eliminated.

**So the correct sentence is- ***Without education we are **incomplete** and our lives are useless without any meaning attached to it.*

His hard (1)/ punch lay (2)/ him on the road . (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'2' i.e. error lies in part 2 of the sentence.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**In part 2 of the sentence**, the usage of **'lay'** is incorrect Instead, use **'laid'**

 
• **According to grammar,** the subject of the sentence is a noun in the given sentence the subject is 'punch' and the object of the sentence is 'him' in the given sentence we need to use the past tense because the action is already performed.
 
• **'lay'** is a transitive verb and the verb of this verb is **'lay⇒ laid⇒ laid⇒ laying' this means 'to put something down'**
 
• Let's see an example-
 
 
• They have laid the table, let's have dinner.
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-** *His hard punch **laid** him on the road.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/11e549cb45ac78aca065082aa5a940b1d6506603cfff2fd1300a22049ad93dc6.png] *

 
• *The verb 'lie' is an intransitive verb and the verb forms of this verb are **'Lie*****⇒ Lay⇒ Lain⇒ Lying*' and the meaning of this verb is 'to fall'***
 
• *Let's see an example-*
 
 
• *​He lays down. (here the verb lays is an intransitive verb and down is an adverb that gives the reply of where?)*
